title: Usher syndrome
summary: Usher syndrome causes hearing loss, often from birth, and sight loss that starts later in childhood or adulthood. Some types also affect balance.
inheritance_plain: It is inherited in an autosomal recessive way: a child is affected only if they get a changed copy of the same gene (one of several linked to it) from both parents.
carrier_meaning: A carrier has one changed copy. Carriers are healthy and usually do not know they are carriers until they are tested.
disease_meaning: A person with two changed copies has Usher syndrome. Hearing aids or cochlear implants, sight support and early communication help make a real difference.
screening: A carrier test uses a blood or saliva sample. It looks for the most common changes and cannot find every possible change.
suggested_questions: Someone in my family has Usher syndrome. Could I be a carrier?
Can Usher syndrome skip a generation?
What does a test for Usher syndrome involve?
card_summary: Hearing loss and sight loss that starts later. Carriers are healthy.
carrier_short: One changed copy. Healthy. Can pass the copy on.
disease_short: Two changed copies. Affects hearing and sight; support makes a real difference.
care: Hearing and eye clinics, cochlear implant centres, genetic counselling and deaf-blind support groups.
